name: Dharmveer Swarajyarakshak Chhatrapati Sambhaji Maharaj Coastal Road
lanes: 8 lanes on the surface sections, with twin tunnels under Malabar Hill

route.start: Marine Drive (Princess Street flyover), Mumbai, Maharashtra

timeline.event: First stretch opens in March; both directions open in stages through the year
Fully open round-the-clock, with the new seaside promenade inaugurated in August

history: Mumbai's Coastal Road is a new expressway built along the city's western shoreline, partly on land reclaimed from the sea and partly through tunnels under Malabar Hill. Built by the city's municipal corporation (BMC), its first phase runs from Marine Drive to Worli, where it joins the Bandra–Worli Sea Link. It opened in stages during 2024 and became fully operational in 2025, cutting a trip that could take close to an hour in traffic down to about ten minutes, and adding a long public promenade beside the sea.
facts: Its twin tunnels pass beneath Girgaum Chowpatty — often described as India's first undersea road tunnels.
The tunnels were dug by 'Mavala', one of the largest tunnel boring machines ever used in India.
Cuts the Marine Drive–Worli drive to around 10 minutes.
Comes with a new public promenade and green space built along the reclaimed shoreline.
